## 📄 06-emails/2026-06-03-bus293-tmd-2026-bus293-0bm-week-4-3626__BUS293_Topic4_Motivation_Presentation.md

# 2026-06-03-bus293-tmd-2026-bus293-0bm-week-4-3626__BUS293_Topic4_Motivation_Presentation

> Конвертировано из `2026-06-03-bus293-tmd-2026-bus293-0bm-week-4-3626__BUS293_Topic4_Motivation_Presentation.pptx`

<!-- Slide number: 1 -->
# Employee Motivation
BUS293 Organisational Theory and Behaviour
Topic 4: Motivation Theories and Applications

<!-- Slide number: 2 -->
# Learning Outcomes
Understand content and process theories of motivation
Apply motivation theories to workplace situations
Explain goal setting and feedback

<!-- Slide number: 3 -->
# What is Motivation?
Motivation drives behaviour and performance.
Employee engagement = emotional commitment + focused effort.
Example: A staff member volunteers for extra projects because they enjoy contributing.

<!-- Slide number: 4 -->
# Content Theories
Focus on WHAT motivates people.
Examples: Maslow, McClelland, Four-Drive Theory.
Example: An employee seeks promotion to satisfy achievement needs.

<!-- Slide number: 5 -->
# Maslow's Hierarchy
Physiological → Safety → Social → Esteem → Self-Actualisation.
Example: Job security motivates a new employee more than leadership opportunities.

<!-- Slide number: 6 -->
# Equity Theory
People compare inputs and rewards with others.
Negative inequity: feeling under-rewarded.
Example: Two employees do similar work, but one receives a larger bonus.

<!-- Slide number: 7 -->
# Organisational Justice
Distributive Justice = fairness of outcomes.
Procedural Justice = fairness of processes.
Example: Transparent promotion criteria improve motivation.

<!-- Slide number: 8 -->
# Expectancy Theory
Motivation depends on:
Expectancy (effort→performance)
Instrumentality (performance→reward)
Valence (value of reward)
Example: Sales staff work harder when bonuses are achievable and valued.

<!-- Slide number: 9 -->
# Reinforcement Theory
Positive Reinforcement: reward good behaviour.
Negative Reinforcement: remove unwanted condition.
Punishment: discourage behaviour.
Extinction: remove rewards for poor behaviour.

<!-- Slide number: 10 -->
# Examples of Reinforcement
Positive: Employee receives recognition.
Negative: Extra supervision removed after improvement.
Punishment: Written warning for misconduct.
Extinction: Stop rewarding lateness.

<!-- Slide number: 11 -->
# Social Cognitive Theory
People learn by observing others.
Example: A new employee learns customer service skills by shadowing a senior colleague.

<!-- Slide number: 12 -->
# Goal Setting Theory
SMARTER Goals:
Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound, Exciting, Reviewed.
Example: Increase customer satisfaction from 80% to 90% within 6 months.

<!-- Slide number: 13 -->
# Effective Feedback
Feedback should be specific, timely, credible and supportive.
Example: 'Your report was accurate and submitted early; keep using this approach.'

<!-- Slide number: 14 -->
# Limitations of Goal Setting
Overemphasis on measurable goals.
Can encourage stress or unethical behaviour.
May hinder learning for new employees.

<!-- Slide number: 15 -->
# Key Takeaways
Motivation is critical for performance.
Fairness, rewards, goals and feedback influence behaviour.
Managers should build capability, provide support and ensure justice.

# 2026-06-03-bus293-tmd-2026-bus293-0bm-week-4-3626__Student_Presentation_Structure

> Конвертировано из `2026-06-03-bus293-tmd-2026-bus293-0bm-week-4-3626__Student_Presentation_Structure.docx`

# Student Presentation Structure (5 Minutes per Group)

## Slide 1: Introduction to the Theory

* Name of the theory
* Founder(s)
* Year developed
* Main purpose of the theory
* Example: Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs developed by Abraham Maslow (1943) explains how human needs motivate behaviour.

## Slide 2: Key Concepts of the Theory

* Define the theory
* Explain the main concepts/components
* Use a diagram or model
* Questions to Answer:
* What does the theory explain?
* What are its main elements?

## Slide 3: How the Theory Works

* Explain the process step-by-step
* Describe how motivation or behaviour occurs according to the theory
* Example for Expectancy Theory: Effort → Performance → Reward → Motivation

## Slide 4: Workplace Example

* Provide a real-life organisational example.
* Example: A company offers performance bonuses to employees who achieve monthly sales targets.

## Slide 5: Application in Organisations

* Discuss how managers can use the theory.
* Questions:
* How can managers apply this theory?
* How can it improve employee performance?
* How can it improve engagement?

## Slide 6: Advantages/Strengths

* Discuss 3–5 strengths.
* Example:
* Easy to understand
* Helps managers identify employee needs
* Useful for employee engagement

## Slide 7: Limitations/Criticisms

* Discuss 3–5 weaknesses.
* Example:
* Not all employees are motivated in the same way
* Difficult to measure some concepts
* Cultural differences may affect applicability

## Slide 8: Modern-Day Example

* Find a company that uses similar principles.
* Examples:
* Google
* Microsoft
* Emirates Airlines
* Amazon
* Apple
* Explain how the company applies the theory.

Dear Students,
I hope you are doing well.
With regard to Assessment 2 (A2) – Team Research Report (30%), please find below a simplified explanation of the assessment requirements to assist you in understanding the task and planning your group work effectively.
The report requires you to work in teams of up to four members,
select one topic from the prescribed list,
and apply it to a suitable organisation listed on either the ASX200 or SGX.
Your report should critically analyse the challenges faced by the chosen organisation in relation to the selected topic, provide evidence-based recommendations for improvement, and demonstrate alignment with at least one of the United Nations Global Compact Principles.
The assessment also requires you to:

  *
Apply relevant organisational behaviour theories and concepts.
  *
Support your arguments with scholarly and credible sources.
  *
Use real-world organisational examples.
  *
Demonstrate teamwork, collaboration, and professional communication skills.
  *
Record all formal group communications through the LMS Team Discussion Forum.

It is your responsibility to ensure that your report fully complies with the requirements outlined in the Unit Outline and LMS resources.
If you have any questions regarding the assessment, please raise them during class
I wish you and your team every success with your report.

# 2026-06-10-bus293-tmd2026-bus293-obm-week-5-10626-wednesday-class__BUS293_Topic5_Class_Presentation

> Конвертировано из `2026-06-10-bus293-tmd2026-bus293-obm-week-5-10626-wednesday-class__BUS293_Topic5_Class_Presentation.pptx`

<!-- Slide number: 1 -->
# Job Satisfaction & Employee Behaviour
BUS293 Organisational Theory and Behaviour
Topic: Job Satisfaction, Emotional Intelligence, Stress & Job Design

<!-- Slide number: 2 -->
# Job Satisfaction
How employees evaluate their jobs.
Dissatisfaction can lead to: Exit, Voice, Loyalty, or Neglect.
Example: A cashier unhappy with workload may resign (Exit) or suggest improvements (Voice).

<!-- Slide number: 3 -->
# Emotional Intelligence (EI)
Self-awareness
Self-management
Social awareness
Relationship management
Example: A supervisor calming an upset customer while supporting staff.

<!-- Slide number: 4 -->
# True Story: Satya Nadella (Microsoft)
After becoming CEO, Nadella emphasized empathy and emotional intelligence.
He transformed Microsoft's culture from internal competition to collaboration.
Result: Improved innovation and company performance.

<!-- Slide number: 5 -->
# Stress at Work
Distress = harmful stress; Eustress = positive, motivating stress.
Common stressors: work overload, low control, workplace conflict.
 Example: Student balancing assignments and part-time work.

<!-- Slide number: 6 -->
# Managing Stress
Remove the stressor
Change perceptions
Seek social support
Flexible work arrangements and work-life balance help reduce stress.

<!-- Slide number: 7 -->
# Job Design Approaches
Job Specialisation – one repetitive task
Job Enlargement – more tasks added
Job Rotation – move between roles
Job Enrichment – more responsibility and autonomy

<!-- Slide number: 8 -->
# True Story: Toyota Job Rotation
Toyota rotates employees across functions.
Employees gain broader skills and understanding.
Result: Higher flexibility, teamwork, and problem-solving capability.

<!-- Slide number: 9 -->
# Job Enrichment Example
Instead of only entering customer data, an employee also follows up with customers and resolves issues.
Benefits: Meaningful work, autonomy, motivation, and satisfaction.

<!-- Slide number: 10 -->
# Key Takeaways
Emotions, stress, rewards, and job design affect satisfaction.
Emotional intelligence can be developed.
Well-designed jobs improve motivation and performance.
Organizations should support employee wellbeing.
